tldr: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Sol on Sep 29, pitching near-Astra intelligence for coding and computer use at one-fifth of Astra's API token prices. On Oct 9 Asana reported its browser agent 76x cheaper and 5x faster in tests.
whats_new: A secondary report says Codex CLI now defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol and cuts price 80%; OpenAI has not confirmed it in this thread.
why_it_matters: GPT-6.1 Sol lowers the price of Astra-class coding and computer-use work, so routing and cost-per-task assumptions built on Astra pricing are out of date.

status.detail: GPT-6.1 Sol has moved from launch to a customer cost claim and a reported Codex CLI default.

beats.headline: GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra's token prices
beats.summary: OpenAI pitches it for coding, computer use and professional work.

beats.headline: Asana reports 76x lower model cost and 5x speed in browser-agent tests
beats.summary: Asana ran the tests with GPT-6 Astra in Codex.

beats.headline: Report: Codex CLI defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol and cuts price 80%

open_questions: Does OpenAI confirm Codex CLI's default switch to GPT-6.1 Sol and the 80% price cut?
Does Asana's 76x cost reduction reproduce outside its browser-agent tests?
How does GPT-6.1 Sol compare with Claude Opus 5.5 on cost per completed task?
take_for_builders: Rerun your coding and computer-use evals on GPT-6.1 Sol against your current Astra baseline, comparing cost per completed task, before changing any default model.
